headline: Obama order sets up a government review of options for detaining people captured in armed conflicts and counterterrorism operations.
what_it_does: This executive order creates a task force of federal agencies to study the legal options for holding people captured in armed conflicts and counterterrorism operations. The task force looks at how such people could be detained, put on trial, moved to other countries, or released. It then reports its recommendations to the President. The order itself orders a review and does not change any detention rules.

who_it_affects.group: People captured or held by the US in armed conflicts or counterterrorism operations
who_it_affects.how: Future policies on how they are held, tried, transferred, or released may be shaped by the review's recommendations.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies such as the Justice Department and Defense Department
who_it_affects.how: Their officials must take part in the task force and produce the review.
